title: Apply customer due diligence measures
summary: Identify the customer and verify identity from a reliable independent source, identify beneficial owners, and assess the purpose and intended nature of the business relationship before establishing it.
addressee: Relevant persons within MLRs 2017 scope (credit/financial institutions, and other regulated sectors)
trigger: Establishing a business relationship; occasional transactions above threshold; any suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing

title: Conduct ongoing monitoring of business relationships
summary: Scrutinise transactions throughout the relationship to ensure consistency with the customer's known risk profile, and keep CDD documents and information up to date.
trigger: Continuously, for the life of every established business relationship

derivation.method: Production: deterministic duty extraction + gated triage; demo: authored against the cited clauses

title: Apply enhanced due diligence in high-risk situations
summary: Apply enhanced due diligence measures and enhanced ongoing monitoring in any case identified as high risk, including high-risk third countries, PEPs, and unusually complex or large transactions.
trigger: High-risk factors present: high-risk third country, politically exposed person, complex/unusually large transaction, or any other higher-risk case

title: Maintain a written business-wide ML/TF risk assessment
summary: Take appropriate steps to identify and assess the money-laundering and terrorist-financing risks the business faces, considering customers, countries, products, transactions and delivery channels, and keep a written record.
trigger: Standing obligation; refreshed when the business or its risk exposure changes

title: Establish AML policies, controls and procedures
summary: Establish and maintain written policies, controls and procedures proportionate to the risk assessment, including internal controls, risk management practices, and where required an independent audit function.
trigger: Standing obligation, proportionate to size and nature of the business

title: Keep CDD and transaction records
summary: Keep copies of customer due diligence documents and supporting transaction records for the prescribed retention period after the end of the relationship or completion of the transaction.
trigger: On every CDD measure and every transaction within scope

title: Process personal data lawfully, fairly and transparently
summary: Every processing operation must satisfy the data-protection principles and rest on a valid lawful basis (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests).
addressee: Controllers (and processors for their duties) processing personal data of EU data subjects

derivation.method: Production: deterministic duty extraction + gated triage; demo: authored against the cited clauses

title: Implement appropriate technical and organisational security measures
summary: Implement measures appropriate to the risk, including pseudonymisation and encryption where appropriate, the ability to ensure confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience, and regular testing of effectiveness.

derivation.method: Production: deterministic duty extraction + gated triage; demo: authored against the cited clauses

title: Notify personal data breaches within 72 hours
summary: Notify the supervisory authority of a personal data breach without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours of becoming aware, unless the breach is unlikely to risk individuals' rights and freedoms.
addressee: Controllers (processors must inform the controller without undue delay)
trigger: Awareness of a personal data breach

title: Carry out data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing
summary: Before processing likely to result in high risk to individuals — in particular large-scale profiling or monitoring — carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing on the protection of personal data.
trigger: New processing likely to result in high risk (large-scale, systematic, sensitive)

title: Maintain records of processing activities
summary: Maintain a written (including electronic) record of processing activities under the organisation's responsibility, covering purposes, categories, recipients, transfers, envisaged time limits and security measures.
addressee: Controllers and processors (with the small-organisation carve-out)
trigger: Standing obligation while processing personal data

title: Designate a data protection officer where required
summary: Designate a DPO where core activities require regular and systematic large-scale monitoring of data subjects or large-scale processing of special-category data, and publish the DPO's contact details.
addressee: Controllers and processors meeting the designation tests
trigger: Core activities meet the Article 37 designation tests

title: Maintain an ICT risk-management framework
summary: Maintain a sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk-management framework, owned by the management body, covering identification, protection, detection, response and recovery for ICT risk.

trigger: Before providing any crypto-asset service in the Union

title: Maintain CASP governance arrangements
